A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Temperature-Annealed Boltzmann Generators by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite formatting changes and substantial additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original sampling experiments on three peptide systems, molecular simulations, and FAB hyperparameter experiments, including Table 1 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains original molecular experiments and adds TA-BG ablations, Gaussian dimension-scaling experiments, runtime measurements, and original Gaussian-mixture sampling results.

M1.justification: The two-stage TA-BG algorithm and molecular flow architecture remain. Appendix C changes the specified regularized energy for E > E_max from E_max to log(E_max - E_high + 1) + E_high, a limited correction to the training loss definition. Whether implementation changed is unstated. The AIS extension in Appendix F.4 is proposed for future use.

E1.justification: The three peptide systems are retained, while v2 extends evaluation beyond molecular distributions with a 40-component two-dimensional Gaussian mixture (Appendix K) and a Gaussian IS/AIS scaling experiment reaching 500 dimensions (Appendix F.4). These add distinct synthetic sampling scenarios, without demonstrating coverage of larger molecular systems.

E2.justification: The molecular comparator set remains forward KLD, reverse KLD, and FAB. The new GMM comparison adds PIS, DDS, iDEM, and Real-NVP FAB alongside neural-spline FAB (Table 15), substantially broadening comparison methods. Appendix K explicitly attributes the diffusion and Real-NVP FAB scores to prior work; they are reported comparisons, not new runs by these authors.

E3.justification: v2 adds controlled annealing sweeps, Gaussian dimension-scaling protocols, and GMM-specific model configurations and evaluation using 1,000 samples per metric. It also revises molecular FAB's reported coordinate range from [-5,5] to [0,10] and initial HMC step size from 0.1 to 0.05 (v1 G.2; v2 G.1). These explicit setting revisions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained FAB ablations and qualitative workflow variations, v2 adds systematic TA-BG tests of direct reweighting, starting temperature, linear versus geometric schedules, final and intermediate fine-tuning, annealing count, and buffer size (F.3). Appendices F.4 and J additionally analyze dimensional scaling and computational cost.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains means and standard errors over four independent experiments. New Table 15 instead reports standard deviations, using four runs for the authors' GMM experiments and three for imported results. Appendix F.3 specifies single runs for most new ablations and four runs per starting temperature. No increase in the main experiments' run count is stated.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results change: Table 1's hexapeptide NLL becomes -501.511 instead of -501.523 for TA-BG, and -501.268 instead of -501.275 for FAB. Substantial new results include hexapeptide ESS of 15.38% versus 7.56% with versus without intermediate fine-tuning, GMM comparisons, and runtime measurements. Main molecular conclusions remain; revised settings prevent interpreting updated scores as demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: New Appendix F.4 introduces an independent-neighborhood clash model and derives expected normalized ESS = (1 - eta)^N, explaining exponential degradation with dimension. Appendix C also corrects the piecewise energy-regularization definition. These are limited mathematical additions and corrections; the main flow and reweighting derivations remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: high-temperature reverse-KLD training avoids mode collapse, iterative reweighting anneals to the target temperature, and molecular experiments achieve strong accuracy with up to threefold fewer energy evaluations. Added appendix evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 substantially qualifies efficiency and scalability. Appendix J explains that additional flow evaluations make TA-BG slower than FAB in the current setup, with anticipated benefits for expensive potentials. Appendix F.4 discusses high-dimensional importance-sampling failure. The discussion adds permutation-invariance limitations, while Appendix K explains the illustrative scope of GMM results and exclusion of symmetric-particle benchmarks.

D1.justification: The Software and Data statement changes from a promised release to concrete GitHub and Zenodo access locations. v2 also documents million-sample validation datasets, cosine scheduling for forward/reverse KLD, regularized-energy use in ESS, GMM implementation settings, and CPU/GPU hardware with timing details. These materially expand reproducibility information; newly disclosed details do not alone establish changed experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and context for diffusion samplers, transition-path sampling, adaptive AIS, and recent flow/protein-ensemble models. The central positioning against MD-dependent temperature-transfer approaches and FAB remains largely unchanged. Publication updates for existing works, such as TRADE, are not new research additions.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain. v2 makes localized explanations of training, annealing, and metrics clearer, standardizes terminology, and reorganizes appendix hyperparameters by method. Acknowledgments and an impact statement are added. The retained narrative is refined rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 5–11 and Tables 6–9, 14, and 15 for ablations, scaling, runtime, and GMM results. Earlier appendix Figures 5–11 correspond to Figures 12–18, with several heatmaps updated. The ICML format also changes typography, title and affiliation layout, headers, captions, reference columns, and table placement throughout.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves important evidence and reporting gaps: Appendix F.3 tests design choices that v1 largely justified verbally, and Appendix J exposes the wall-time tradeoff behind energy-evaluation savings. Scaling limitations, implementation details, and concrete code/data locations improve interpretation and reproducibility. Most new ablations remain single-run and the Gaussian tests are limited demonstrations, but the stronger empirical justification and more transparent costs substantially improve overall quality.
